title: Habitat Connectivity
description: A compilation of landscape-connectivity and climate-resilience GIS layers for California, combining CDFW wildlife-connectivity and barrier datasets with published climate-adaptation connectivity models (Beier 2006, Schloss 2022, Cameron 2022). ## README.md
# public-connectivity

Landscape **connectivity & climate-resilience** datasets for California, from the California Biodiversity Network (CBN) and partners. All products are cloud-native and served from NRP S3 (`https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/`).

| Dataset | Source | Products | License |
|---|---|---|---|
| `regional-connectivity-linkages` | Beier et al. 2006 — South Coast Missing Linkages (CDFW BIOS ds419) | GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex (res 8) | CC-BY-4.0 |
| `wildlife-movement-barriers` | CDFW 2024 — Terrestrial Wildlife Connectivity Barriers (BIOS ds2867) | GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex (res 8) | CC-BY-4.0 |
| `climate-migration-routes` | Schloss et al. 2022 (Dryad `d7wm37q1m`) | COG, H3 hex (res 9) | CC0-1.0 |
| `present-day-connectivity/flow` | Cameron et al. 2022 (Dryad `7sqv9s4v3`) | COG, H3 hex (res 9) | CC0-1.0 |
| `present-day-connectivity/categories` | Cameron et al. 2022 (Dryad `7sqv9s4v3`) | COG, H3 hex (res 9) | CC0-1.0 |

All layers are in **OGC:CRS84 / EPSG:4326**. The three raster sources were reprojected from their native ESRI:102003 (USA Contiguous Albers) / sphere Web-Mercator projections to EPSG:4326 (categorical layers with nearest-neighbor; the continuous flow index with bilinear).

---

## Vector — regional-connectivity-linkages (Beier 2006)

11 South Coast Missing Linkages polygons (e.g. Tehachapi, Sierra Madre – Castaic).

**DuckDB:**
```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SELECT Proj_Name, Area_ha
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/regional-connectivity-linkages.parquet')
ORDER BY Area_ha DESC;
```

**MapLibre GL JS** (PMTiles — note the `source-layer` is `regional-connectivity-linkages`):
```js
map.addSource('linkages', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/regional-connectivity-linkages.pmtiles' });
map.addLayer({
  id: 'linkages-fill', type: 'fill',
  source: 'linkages',
  'source-layer': 'regional-connectivity-linkages',
  paint: { 'fill-color': '#2c7fb8', 'fill-opacity': 0.5 }
});
```

**H3 hex** (res 8). Area columns are per-feature totals repeated on every cell — never `SUM` them on hex; dedup by `_cng_fid`, or compute area from `COUNT(DISTINCT h8) × cell_area_at_res_8`:
```sql
SELECT Proj_Name, COUNT(DISTINCT h8) AS cells
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/regional-connectivity-linkages/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;
```

---

## Vector — wildlife-movement-barriers (CDFW 2024)

204 linear infrastructure segments (roads/highways) that CDFW identified as barriers to terrestrial wildlife movement across California, with priority rankings for 2020/2022/2024 and remediation status. Source: CDFW BIOS **ds2867** (priorities as of June 2024). Geometry is **lines** (LineString / MultiLineString); each segment was hexed to H3 resolution 8 by buffering it by the H3 cell circumradius before polyfill.

**DuckDB** — top-priority barriers by length:
```sql
INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial;
SELECT Barrier_ID, Segment_Name, County, Priority_2024, Length_kilometers
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/wildlife-movement-barriers.parquet')
WHERE Priority_2024 = 'Top Priority Barrier'
ORDER BY Length_kilometers DESC;
```

**MapLibre GL JS** (PMTiles — note the `source-layer` is `wildlife-movement-barriers`):
```js
map.addSource('barriers', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/wildlife-movement-barriers.pmtiles' });
map.addLayer({
  id: 'barriers-line', type: 'line',
  source: 'barriers',
  'source-layer': 'wildlife-movement-barriers',
  paint: {
    'line-width': 2,
    'line-color': [
      'match', ['get', 'Priority_2024'],
      'Top Priority Barrier', '#d7301f',
      'Priority Barrier', '#fc8d59',
      'Barrier', '#fdcc8a',
      'Remediated', '#2c7fb8',
      '#cccccc'
    ]
  }
});
```

**H3 hex** (res 8). `Length_kilometers` is a per-feature total **repeated on every cell** a barrier covers — never `SUM` it on hex; dedup by `Barrier_ID` (one row per barrier) or `_cng_fid` first, or count barriers with `COUNT(DISTINCT Barrier_ID)`:
```sql
-- barriers per H3 cell (where wildlife corridors are most pinched)
SELECT h8, COUNT(DISTINCT Barrier_ID) AS n_barriers
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/wildlife-movement-barriers/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY h8 ORDER BY n_barriers DESC;
```

`Priority_2020`/`Priority_2022`/`Priority_2024` take values `Barrier`, `Priority Barrier`, `Top Priority Barrier`, `Remediated` (NULL = not assessed that cycle). `Target_Species` is a free-text, comma-separated list of focal species. `CDFW_Region` is 1–6 (comma-joined for barriers spanning multiple regions). `SUMMARY_LINK` is a per-barrier CDFW summary PDF.

---

## Rasters

H3 hex tables have columns `<value>`, `h9` (native res 9), `h0` (partition key). One row per H3 cell.

### climate-migration-routes (Schloss 2022) — categorical, 13 classes
Connectivity class per cell (`mode` reducer). Classes: `0` limited/none; `100–103` Diffuse (intact); `200–203` Intensified (multiple linkages); `300–303` Channelized (present-day linkage); `+1/+2/+3` = HADGEM2-ES / CNRM-CM5 / both climate-model linkages. See `classification:classes` on the COG band.

```sql
SELECT connectivity_class, COUNT(*) n
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/climate-migration-routes/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```
COG (titiler / categorical colormap): `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/climate-migration-routes-cog.tif`

### present-day-connectivity/flow (Cameron 2022) — continuous index 0–100
Current-flow connectivity index (`mean` reducer).
```sql
SELECT MIN(current_flow), MAX(current_flow), AVG(current_flow)
FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/present-day-connectivity-flow/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet');
```
COG: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/present-day-connectivity-flow-cog.tif`

### present-day-connectivity/categories (Cameron 2022) — categorical, 12 classes
Connectivity-strategy category per cell (`mode` reducer). Classes: `3` Limited movement potential; `4` Permeable (local movement); `19` Impeded; `25,29` Diffuse; `31,35,39` Intensified; `41,45,49` Channelized; `0` background (undocumented in source). See `classification:classes` on the COG band.
COG: `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-connectivity/present-day-connectivity-categories-cog.tif`

---

## Citations
- California Department of Fish and Wildlife (2024). Terrestrial Wildlife Connectivity Barriers (Wildlife Movement Barriers). CDFW BIOS ds2867. https://wildlife.ca.gov/Data/BIOS
- Beier, P., et al. (2006). South Coast Missing Linkages. South Coast Wildlands. (CDFW BIOS ds419)
- Cameron, D. R., Schloss, C. A., Theobald, D. M., & Morrison, S. A. (2022). A framework to select strategies for conserving and restoring habitat connectivity. *Conservation Science and Practice*, e12698. https://doi.org/10.1111/csp2.12698
- Schloss, C. A., et al. (2022). "No-regrets" pathways for navigating climate change. *Ecological Applications*. https://doi.org/10.1002/eap.2468
